People also ask
How much is a cow in Nigeria in 2026?
An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
AI Overview

AI Mode replied:

In 2026, the price of a
cow
in Nigeria ranges wildly from ₦150,000 for a very small calf to ₦2.5 million for premium, giant-sized breeds. Livestock prices have escalated drastically due to inflation, high fuel and transportation costs, and security challenges along transit routes. 
Average Price Breakdown by Size
Cattle markets categorize pricing predominantly by the animal's physical size and weight: 
  • Small Cow / Calf: ₦150,000 – ₦350,000
  • Medium-Sized Cow: ₦400,000 – ₦800,000
  • Large / Standard Event Cow: ₦850,000 – ₦1.5 million
  • Giant / Premium Fattened Breed (e.g., Sokoto Gudali, Bokolo):
    ₦1.6 million – ₦2.5 million
     
Key Factors Driving the 2026 Market
  • Geographic Location: Cows are drastically cheaper in northern states (the primary rearing hubs). Prices spike heavily in southern metropolitan hubs like Lagos and Port Harcourt due to added logistics costs. 
  • Butcher Crises: According to reports from the Lagos State Butchers Association, premium cows reaching ₦2.5 million have actually made some cattle more expensive than locally used cars, severely stressing market vendors. 
  • Festivity Rushes: Prices surge significantly during major festive seasons like Eid al-Kabir (Sallah) and December holiday periods due to a sudden drop in available supply against high consumer demand. 
If you are planning a purchase, would you like advice on how to negotiate at local livestock markets or tips on crowdsourcing/sharing a cow to save money?
